passages.text: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is the beloved.
The beloved speaks to his bride.
He calls her his sister and his bride.
He says, "I have come to my garden."
He says, "I have gathered my myrrh with my spice."
He says, "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey."
He says, "I have drunk my wine with my milk."
He invites his friends.
He says, "Eat, friends."
He says, "Drink, beloved ones."
He says, "Drink freely."
passages.original: בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ אָרִ֤יתִי מוֹרִי֙ עִם־ בְּשָׂמִ֔י אָכַ֤לְתִּי יַעְרִי֙ עִם־ דִּבְשִׁ֔י שָׁתִ֥יתִי יֵינִ֖י עִם־ חֲלָבִ֑י אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים שְׁת֥וּ וְשִׁכְר֖וּ דּוֹדִֽים׃ס

passages.text: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
passages.sermon:
I am lying down to sleep.
My body rests.
But my heart stays awake.
I hear a sound.
My beloved knocks at the door.
He calls to me.
He says, "Open the door for me.
You are my sister.
You are my beloved.
You are my dove.
You are perfect to me.
My head is wet with dew.
My hair is damp from the night."
passages.original: אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה וְלִבִּ֣י עֵ֑ר ק֣וֹל׀ דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק פִּתְחִי־ לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י שֶׁרֹּאשִׁי֙ נִמְלָא־ טָ֔ל קְוֻּצּוֹתַ֖י רְסִ֥יסֵי לָֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: I have taken off my robe— must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks.
She has removed her robe.
She asks, “Must I put my robe back on?”
She has washed her feet.
She asks, “Must I make my feet dirty again?”
passages.original: פָּשַׁ֙טְתִּי֙ אֶת־ כֻּתָּנְתִּ֔י אֵיכָ֖כָה אֶלְבָּשֶׁ֑נָּה רָחַ֥צְתִּי אֶת־ רַגְלַ֖י אֵיכָ֥כָה אֲטַנְּפֵֽם׃

passages.text: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.
passages.sermon:
My beloved reached his hand through the opening.
He touched the latch.
My heart pounded for him.
I felt deep longing for him.
passages.original: דּוֹדִ֗י שָׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ מִן־ הַחֹ֔ר וּמֵעַ֖י הָמ֥וּ עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
passages.sermon:
The woman loved her beloved deeply.
She got up to open the door for him.
Her hands dripped with myrrh.
Her fingers dripped with flowing myrrh.
The myrrh touched the handles of the bolt.
passages.original: קַ֥מְתִּֽי אֲנִ֖י לִפְתֹּ֣חַ לְדוֹדִ֑י וְיָדַ֣י נָֽטְפוּ־ מ֗וֹר וְאֶצְבְּעֹתַי֙ מ֣וֹר עֹבֵ֔ר עַ֖ל כַּפּ֥וֹת הַמַּנְעֽוּל׃

passages.text: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him, but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.
passages.sermon:
The woman loved her beloved deeply.
She opened the door for her beloved.
Her beloved had already turned away.
He was gone.
Her heart felt empty when he left.
She looked for him.
She did not find him.
She called out to him.
He did not answer her.
passages.original: פָּתַ֤חְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ לְדוֹדִ֔י וְדוֹדִ֖י חָמַ֣ק עָבָ֑ר נַפְשִׁי֙ יָֽצְאָ֣ה בְדַבְּר֔וֹ בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֙יהוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מְצָאתִ֔יהוּ קְרָאתִ֖יו וְלֹ֥א עָנָֽנִי׃

passages.text: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.
passages.sermon:
The watchmen patrol the city.
I met the watchmen.
They beat me.
They wounded me.
The watchmen took my cloak from me.
These watchmen guard the walls.
passages.original: מְצָאֻ֧נִי הַשֹּׁמְרִ֛ים הַסֹּבְבִ֥ים בָּעִ֖יר הִכּ֣וּנִי פְצָע֑וּנִי נָשְׂא֤וּ אֶת־ רְדִידִי֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman in Jerusalem.
She addresses the daughters of Jerusalem.
She urges them strongly.
She says, “If you find my beloved, tell him this.”
She says, “I am sick with love.”
passages.original: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אִֽם־ תִּמְצְאוּ֙ אֶת־ דּוֹדִ֔י מַה־ תַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ שֶׁחוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so?
passages.sermon:
The daughters of Jerusalem speak to the woman.
They see that she is the most beautiful among women.
They ask her a question.
They say, “How is your beloved better than other men?”
They ask, “How is your beloved better than another?”
They want to know why she makes them promise in this way.
passages.original: מַה־ דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים מַה־ דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד שֶׁכָּ֖כָה הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks about her beloved.
She says her beloved is dazzling.
He is also ruddy.
He stands out among ten thousand people.
He is outstanding and unique.

passages.text: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
passages.sermon:
The beloved man stands out among many.
His head shines like pure gold.
His hair is wavy.
His hair is black like a raven.
passages.original: רֹאשׁ֖וֹ כֶּ֣תֶם פָּ֑ז קְוּצּוֹתָיו֙ תַּלְתַּלִּ֔ים שְׁחֹר֖וֹת כָּעוֹרֵֽב׃

passages.text: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.
passages.sermon:
My beloved is dazzling and ruddy.  
He stands out among ten thousand.  
His eyes are gentle and pure.  
His eyes are like doves.  
The doves rest beside streams of water.  
His eyes are clean and bright, as if washed in milk.  
His eyes are set in his face like precious jewels.
passages.original: עֵינָ֕יו כְּיוֹנִ֖ים עַל־ אֲפִ֣יקֵי מָ֑יִם רֹֽחֲצוֹת֙ בֶּֽחָלָ֔ב יֹשְׁב֖וֹת עַל־ מִלֵּֽאת׃

passages.text: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
passages.sermon:
The man is the beloved.
His cheeks are like beds of spice.
His cheeks are like towers filled with perfume.
His lips are like lilies.
His lips drip with flowing myrrh.
passages.original: לְחָיָו֙ כַּעֲרוּגַ֣ת הַבֹּ֔שֶׂם מִגְדְּל֖וֹת מֶרְקָחִ֑ים שִׂפְתוֹתָיו֙ שֽׁוֹשַׁנִּ֔ים נֹטְפ֖וֹת מ֥וֹר עֹבֵֽר׃

passages.text: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is an ivory panel bedecked with sapphires.
passages.sermon:
The man is the beloved.
His arms are strong.
His arms are like rods of gold.
His arms have beryl set in them.
His body is beautiful.
His body is like a panel of ivory.
His body is covered with sapphires.
passages.original: יָדָיו֙ גְּלִילֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב מְמֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּתַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ מֵעָיו֙ עֶ֣שֶׁת שֵׁ֔ן מְעֻלֶּ֖פֶת סַפִּירִֽים׃

passages.text: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.
passages.sermon:
The man is strong and majestic.
His legs are like pillars of marble.
Pure gold forms the bases under his legs.
He looks like the mountains of Lebanon.
He is as tall and noble as the cedar trees.
passages.original: שׁוֹקָיו֙ עַמּ֣וּדֵי שֵׁ֔שׁ מְיֻסָּדִ֖ים עַל־ אַדְנֵי־ פָ֑ז מַרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ כַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן בָּח֖וּר כָּאֲרָזִֽים׃

passages.text: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks about her beloved.
She says his mouth is very sweet.
She says he is completely lovely.
She calls him her beloved.
She calls him her friend.
She speaks to the daughters of Jerusalem.
passages.original: חִכּוֹ֙ מַֽמְתַקִּ֔ים וְכֻלּ֖וֹ מַחֲמַדִּ֑ים זֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ וְזֶ֣ה רֵעִ֔י בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
